## Historical audit: S0117

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/results/r2/sceneevolve_cli/C1/test/commons_16007442/trajectory.jsonl`. Only chunk 3 is available. All character ranges below are half-open ranges of the cited JSONL line.

| Evidence | Observation and interpretation |
|---|---|
| Student `model_request`, line 22 [0,312033) | **Goal:** reconstruct a single photograph as an editable SceneAct/Blender scene, matching camera, placement, occlusion and materials. The student interpreted it as an electronics workbench; this semantic interpretation is not independently verified because the photograph itself is not visible in this audit. |
| Same event | **Actual builds:** three complete programs describe separate architecture, monitor, scope, meters, keyboard, drawers, lamp, soldering station and leads. Colored primitive meshes provide material distinctions, but no image texture or procedural surface texture is evident. Parts are grouped and positioned, with rotations for the monitor, keyboard, meter and lamp shade; grouping and intended contacts do not prove geometric connection or correct pose. |
| Same event, step 1–3 harness feedback | **Validation:** each execution reports `ok: true`, a finished render and saved Blender scene. These are technical build successes, not proof of visual or geometric fidelity. Render paths are present, but the images themselves are unavailable here. |
| Same event, student revision comments and programs | **Autonomous iteration:** after step 1 the student diagnosed overly wide framing, lateral perspective and washed-out surfaces; step 2 reversed camera offset, increased lens 44→50, enlarged the monitor and lamp, and reduced lighting. After step 2 the student diagnosed low instruments, monitor cropping/perspective and a thin lamp; step 3 lowered the camera target, repositioned and rotated the monitor, and reshaped the lamp. These are student diagnoses and executed changes, not independently confirmed improvements. |
| Student `codex_session`, line 23 [0,4298); `model_response`, line 24 [0,346); `select`, line 25 [0,59) | The final read-only session was supplied the reference and three renders, had zero tool calls, and returned `SELECT 3`; the recorded selection is step 3. The trace does not expose its comparative reasoning or independently establish that step 3 was strongest. |

**Teacher input:** No distinct teacher detection, diagnosis, proposed update, or teacher-to-student receipt is visible in this chunk. The system’s reconstruction procedure and harness prompts were actually supplied; subsequent camera and lighting revisions are consistent with them, but cannot establish adoption of any unseen teacher advice.

**Outcome and uncertainty:** Formal execution and selection succeeded; overall reconstruction correctness is **unknown**, not a demonstrated visual success. There is no visible empty patch, algorithm failure, or technical interruption. Whether objects match the photograph, their parts touch correctly, and final camera, lighting, textures, occlusions and render quality are accurate remains unresolved. The student’s reported camera and washed-out-lighting problems are hypotheses supported only by its own comments here.

**Lessons:** Transferably, separate render/build success from fidelity and compare camera-wide versus local discrepancies before revising. Task-specific hypotheses concern this workbench’s monitor framing, lamp angle and surface brightness; their effectiveness cannot be established without inspecting the actual images.
